title: Meeting Armstrong on Louisiana Avenue, summer 1930
summary: Working at Parish Royal on the lake, Alcorn hears of Louis packing the Suburban Garden and they meet one night on Louisiana Avenue in 1929-30.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And I had a chance to meet Louis. Well, I... How it really came about... I was working at a place called the Parish Royal. It's one of those... Swimming camps out on the lake. Mm-hmm. There was a little clarinet player Lorenzo Teo. A gentleman called Dugas, Ray Dugas. And... Walter Dugas, Piano player. And myself. And we had a couple of Bocais with us. Henry and Charlie Bocais. And we were all working out at the... At the lake. At this place, the Parish Royal. Somewhere out there where... Close to where the airport was located. And Louis... People used to go out... To the suburban garden and listen to Louis. Well, it was in the summertime. It was real hot. It didn't have air conditioning. It didn't have nothing. It just didn't have any pain. People used to go out there. And every night Louis was packing that place up. And if he was packing it in. They used to have a broadcast that would come on at 12 o'clock. At nine? Yeah. Somewhere around that time. And it broadcast Louis from the suburban garden. And quite a few of those people used to come out to the lake. And do air. When the... You know, if they come off... Got that hot place to go out to the lake to swim and cool off. They used to come... This was one of the spots they used to come to too. Mm-hm. from the San Buenville. And quite a few of those people used to come out to the lake and do air. When, you know, if they come off, got that hot place to go out to the lake to swim and cool off, they used to come, this was one of the spots they used to come to too. So quite a few people used to go out and tell them, they say, man, they got a young guy around here playing for a man, he playing some horn, you ought to hear him. And they'll say, yeah, I'd like to meet him. So we made, we set up an appointment to meet each other one night. It must have been about, it wasn't good night or it was next morning. It was about three o'clock. The building was getting off at about 12, 31 o'clock out there.
And I met him. You went from the lakefront over to the suburban?

Yeah, well, I met him in Uptown, because I always lived around Louisiana Avenue up in the city. So it was no hassle. I knew where he used to go at night. Man, you know, it was at that time. Where would they go after the suburban garden? They'd go jam someplace? No, no, they wouldn't jam. They'd go around at the time. They'd go around. And they'd go around. And they'd go around. So I met him one night. Do you remember exactly which place it was? Tickle House. Yeah. No, we first met on the, it was on Losing Avenue in Magnolia. Right there on the corner. right there on the corner. He was in his, he had a little, a little Ford, a sport mile of Ford. And he was sitting in the corner, I went over and I told him where I was. And we started talking and everything. But we had a nice conversation from that time on, you see. And he told me he'd like to hear me and everything. I told him, I said, well you can hear me, you can't come out to the lake, and you can't come out there because you're working like I am, you see. And we had-
Do you remember what year this was, exactly? Oh, um, yeah. 1930.
Yeah, that's 29 or 30. Around 30 or 29 up in there. Yeah, it'd be exactly the early part of, the last part of the 20s and the first part of the 30s, you see.
So this was the summer of 1930, you think? Yeah. Somewhere around up in there. Well, I guess the Depression had just begun by then.
